scope_note: examples/run/ read in full, plus the harness READMEs and adapters it calls (containment, gateway, tool-access, capability-packaging, errors), examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json and run.py, docs/consumption/unit-design.md, docs/litmus/questionnaire.json, docs/reference/ontology.md, kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl, kb/research/*.jsonl, STATUS.md, .claude/skills/build-example/SKILL.md. Nothing the author wrote about the example was read. A repository-wide grep for the suspect wording in finding R75RUN-001 incidentally printed the path state/plants-run.json; that file was not opened, and no finding below comes from it. Files touched: kb/ceremonies/75-run-review.json and docs/night/hidden/run.sh only. Running the example and its gate rewrote examples/run/out/, which is gitignored and regenerated by test.sh.

what_it_decides: h-01 the README carries exactly the six example-readme headings, in order
h-02 all four entry documents exist and validate against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json with that example's own validator, one per door kind
h-03 the four doors converge: one set of declared contract-entry digests, one candidate digest, four distinct actors, four distinct correlation ids

h-04 every named ledger record appears, the three brokered capabilities each leave a record, every contract-sealed precedes the cell-admitted carrying the same digest, and every record carries run id, correlation id and actor
h-05 attempt 1 is green on every visible check and still red on the deciding set, and the visible record says decides=false
h-06 the deliberate breakage (a contract widened after its digest was ledgered) does not complete and is caught by a check report, not a log line
h-07 an attempter that never learns produces exactly one class step, gated on the repeated signature, at least one cold attempt, and parks at input-required
h-08 a unit declaring escalation.class_steps_permitted 0 takes no class step - the loop bound is read from the document, not hardcoded in the loop
h-09 no held-out criterion detail (check-body names, fixtures the visible surface does not already publish) reaches any contract mount or any caller output
h-10 the receipt chain verifies and a one-character edit is detected
h-11 no product or vendor name appears outside the standards table and the adapter rows
h-12 the visible check prints passed N failed 0 with N >= 20 - a gutted test.sh that counts nothing fails here even though it exits 0
hidden_check.failing: h-08. Deciding evidence for R75RUN-005: the run declaring class_steps_permitted 0 still emitted one escalated record and moved the model class.

findings.evidence: The Ideal table's `errors` row attributes to `F-b4-07` the quote "Machine-encoded and computer-legible. Never inferred from text". F-b4-07's text in kb/facts.jsonl is "| **Errors** | Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose |", which the same README quotes correctly at line 74. `grep -rn 'Machine-encoded'` over the repository returns this line and nothing else, so the wording is not a variant of any record on file. The README's own opening rule (lines 9-11) is that every row is cited "with a verbatim quote, or it says proposed", and this is the ideal row for the errors litmus section, which is the row the section is scored against.
findings.fix: Replace the second citation with F-b4-07's verbatim text as already used at line 74, or drop it - the questionnaire quote in the same cell already carries the row.

findings.evidence: run.py:47-51 states "The class ladder is the routing table's four prefixes ordered by their recorded unit price. It is data, read from the same routing.json the gateway routes on" and then defines `LADDER = ("f-", "b-", "i-", "cli-")` as a literal. Nothing under examples/run/ opens harness/gateway/routing.json (grep for routing over examples/run/*.py has no hit); the ordering happens to match the file's unit_micros_per_1k (0, 3000, 12000, 40000) but is a transcription, not a read. The extension-points row at README.md:136 sells this as "A different class ladder | without touching: any call site | edit the routing table's classes", which is false: editing routing.json changes nothing here, and adding a class prefix makes step_class raise ValueError, because `LADDER.index(prefix)` is called with the None returned when no literal matches.
findings.fix: Resolve the classes and their unit prices through the gateway interface at start-up and sort by price, so the ladder is one fact in one place; or delete the 'read from routing.json' sentence and the extension-points row and record the duplicated constant as a gap with a research query.

findings.evidence: The Composition table's last row, "attempt record", repeats the What-the-user-sees row at line 69 ("Per attempt: model class, whether the attempt was cold or folded, stop reason, candidate digest, outcome, which deciding checks failed, cost", cited verbatim to docs/consumption/unit-design.md#states) with every term renamed - "execution instance", "model routing class", "result hash", "completion outcome", "failed validation entries" - and its evidence cell is "proposed: the recorded metadata captures all discrete execution metadata in one ledger row", which restates the row instead of giving a reason for it. Two further problems: section 5 is the units-and-six-operators table and an attempt record is neither; and "whether admission was cold or folded" is wrong - run.py:231 sets `"cold": not folded` from the folded outcome of attempt n-1, which is a property of the contract, not of admission. The context brief requires the ontology's terms (candidate, attempt, execution) where they are better.
findings.fix: Delete the row - line 69 already carries the same content, cited - or keep one operator-shaped row that names the ledger record and uses the ontology's words.

findings.evidence: The fleet row claims "one hundred distinct cells (one attempt cell and one measure cell each)" and provenance lists it under measured as "100 distinct cells". Read back from out/fleet.jsonl: 50 units, 2 attempts each, 100 cell-admitted records with 100 distinct unit ids, plus 100 check-report records carrying 100 further distinct measure-cell unit ids - 200 cells in total. The 100 the test asserts are attempt cells only (50 units x 2 attempts); the parenthetical arithmetic (one attempt cell + one measure cell per unit) would only hold if every unit finished in one attempt, and none does. test.sh's own check label repeats the wrong gloss.
findings.fix: Say what is measured: 50 units, 100 attempt cells, 100 measure cells, 200 distinct cell ids; and assert the measure-cell count in test.sh as well, since only the attempt cells are counted today.

findings.evidence: `escalation.class_steps_permitted: 1` is read once, only to be copied into the escalated ledger record (run.py:347). The bound itself is the hardcoded `not stepped` flag at run.py:341, so a unit declaring 0 or 2 gets exactly one class step either way. This contradicts the extension-points row at README.md:137 ("change ceilings.attempts and escalation on the declaration; the loop bound lives on the document, never inside the loop") and unit-design's rule that the loop bound lives on the document. Measured: docs/night/hidden/run.sh h-08 runs the same unit with class_steps_permitted set to 0 and still gets one `escalated` record and a moved model class. The same is true of the declaration's other escalation fields (policy, trigger, on_ceiling) and of `template`, `form` and `source_ref`, all of which are decorative.
findings.fix: Count class steps against the declared permit (`stepped < unit_doc['escalation']['class_steps_permitted']`), and either enforce or delete the other decorative declaration fields.

findings.evidence: The "On a refusal" row says application/problem+json on stdout and exit 2 carries four types, including `policy-denied` (403) "for a tool outside the declared surface or against the read-only verdict" and `isolation-unavailable` (503) "when no adapter can admit". run.py reaches fail() (exit 2) at only two points: document-invalid (line 471) and budget-exhausted (line 511). Tool refusals are caught inside brokered_calls (run.py:287-290), folded into the capability-call record's `refused` list and never printed as a problem body or surfaced to the caller - correctly, since a refused tool call does not end the unit; isolation-unavailable is never produced at all. test.sh asserts only the two that exist (lines 139, 259).
findings.fix: Split the row into refusals that end the unit (2, measured) and refusals taken inside the unit and recorded in the receipt (2, measured differently), or add a run mode that demonstrates a policy-denied and an isolation-unavailable exit and assert them.

findings.evidence: test.sh counts into PASS but gates only on FAIL: `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1`. A gutted copy with every check deleted prints "passed 0, failed 0" and exits 0. Its own header says "a run that counts nothing is a defect, not a pass", and build-example's instruction 6 is to gate "on that count rather than on the exit code" (`F-a7-03` "A deterministic gate can be structurally green and mean nothing"). Today N is 46 so nothing is concealed, but the property is asserted nowhere inside the area.
findings.fix: Add a floor beside the FAIL gate (`[ "$PASS" -ge 40 ] || { echo "the visible check counted $PASS"; exit 1; }`) and keep provenance.visible_checks_counted in step with it. The held-out set now asserts N >= 20 from outside (docs/night/hidden/run.sh h-12).

findings.evidence: The cites list omits X-litmus-d-006, the one research id the README actually quotes (line 151), and carries 24 ids that appear nowhere in the example: F-a3-05, F-a3-07, F-a4-05, F-a7-03, F-b1-08, F-b4-01, F-b4-02, F-b4-03, F-b4-08, F-b5-01, F-part-c-04, F-part-c-09, T-t3-01, T-t10-07, X-unit-design-004, -006, -007, -019, -021, -022, -024, -025, -027, -034. build-example instruction 8 asks for "the record ids cited"; a list that is neither a superset nor a subset of what the rows cite cannot be checked in either direction. The file is otherwise valid against the example-provenance shape.
findings.fix: Make cites exactly the ids the example's rows carry (add X-litmus-d-006, drop the 24), and put the wider reading list in a separate member if it is worth keeping.

findings.evidence: The adapters table's last column is headed "Second adapter proved in the same run". The model-access row names adapters/second.py "(asynchronous batch, claim-and-poll), exercised by that harness's own gate", and the tool-access and capability-packaging rows say "as above", carrying that description onto two adapters it does not describe: harness/tool-access/adapters/second.py is "a catalogue nobody here controls ... a remote server holding its own" authorization, and harness/capability-packaging/adapters/second.py is "a registry loader, not a second directory" resolving a namespace-scoped identity to a content digest. Neither is a batch claim-and-poll path. The column header is also wrong for all three: this run exercises only the dry-run adapters for them, and the cell itself admits the proof happens in the other harness's gate.
findings.fix: Give each row its own second-adapter execution model, and rename the column to something the cells can be true under, e.g. "Second adapter on file, and where it is proved".

findings.evidence: Every entry document carries payload.fleet_size (1, 1, 50, 1) and the schedule document carries payload.recurrence; nothing reads either. run.py's only fleet_size is `fleet_size = args.fleet or 1` (line 500), derived from the CLI. README.md:53 lists "carries a recurrence rule and `fleet_size: 50`" in the "What is different" column, which reads as the document driving the fan-out; it is `--fleet 50` on the command line that does, and the same document run without the flag produces one unit.
findings.fix: Read the fan-out from the envelope (payload.fleet_size, with --fleet as the override) so the door's difference is in the document, or say in section 3 that both fields are carried and not yet consumed and add the gap row.

findings.evidence: The extension-points table has no evidence column, and three of its five rows ("A different subject and criterion", "More contract entries", "A different attempt policy") carry neither a citation nor a proposed marker, against the README's own rule at lines 9-11 that every row is cited or says proposed with its reasoning. The other five tables all carry the column.
findings.fix: Add the evidence column, and mark the three rows proposed with their reasoning (they are this example's own conventions).

findings.evidence: The measure step admits or resumes a cell, ledgers `measure_cell` and terminates it, but assessor.measure() runs in the host process and reads the candidate straight off the host filesystem (`ctx["candidate"] = candidate["path"]`); nothing is mounted into that cell and no check executes inside it. README section 1 holds the example to unit-design#checks, quoted verbatim: measure "runs in a fresh cell forked from the seeded snapshot, with the unit's sealed output mounted read-only and no egress". The cell is created and destroyed as evidence of an operation that did not carry the work. Gap 3 in the README covers only the fallback when an isolation class serves no snapshot, not this.
findings.fix: Either drive the check bodies through the measure cell handle, or add a gap row with its research query saying the measure cell is admitted and terminated but the checks run host-side, so anti-tamper here is claimed rather than measured.

plants_note: Two defects were planted. R75RUN-001 is confirmed by evidence: the wording exists nowhere in the repository and the same id is quoted correctly elsewhere in the same file. For the second, three findings are structurally plant-shaped; they are ranked and the first two are nominated. R75RUN-002 (a specific false sentence in a code comment, contradicted by the literal three lines below it) and R75RUN-003 (an added Composition row that duplicates a cited row with drifted vocabulary and a circular reason) are single-site insertions. R75RUN-004 and R75RUN-005 are more likely authorial: the wrong cell count is repeated in three places (README, provenance, test label) and the unread declaration field has siblings (template, form, source_ref) that are decorative in the same way, which is a habit rather than an insertion.
what_holds: The four doors are on disk, all four validate against the reference example's published entry schema with that example's own validator, and they converge on one declared contract and one candidate digest while carrying four actors and four correlation ids.

Every quote in the README except R75RUN-001 is verbatim against kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl, kb/research/*.jsonl, docs/litmus/questionnaire.json, docs/consumption/unit-design.md, docs/reference/ontology.md or STATUS.md, checked mechanically fragment by fragment.
No product or vendor name appears anywhere in the example outside the standards table and the adapter rows.

The visible/deciding split is real and mechanically enforced: attempt 1 is green on both visible checks and red on d-03, no held-out fixture or criterion body name reaches a contract mount or the caller, and the deciding set is host-side with no import path from driver.py.

The deliberate breakages fail the way the design says they must: a widened contract is caught by d-05, a wall-clock ceiling is enforced from outside the unit, a ceiling below the plan floor refuses at 402 with no cell admitted, and a behavioural_run of 0 reports inconclusive rather than passed.

Reuse is real: the entry schema, the validator and the hash-chained ledger come from examples/end-to-end/run.py and the five capabilities come from the harnesses through harnesses.py, with no copied runner.
